title.narrative: Research Stream No: 2: Trends in Global Food Security · Two events, with acknowledgement that an event may be substituted for one podcast and/or one written piece and/or one video upon agreement. · Subject matter will include the development of resilient food systems that can withstand the threats of climate change, disease, and conflict through strong value chains and increased access to nutritious foods.

Output indicators for a public event include in-person attendance and live viewership (online), continued viewership of event recordings, media presence, press mentions, engagement with educational materials, and references to the event discussion by experts in the field.
Output indicators for a private event include the number of public and private sector organizations represented during the discussion, the quality of the discussion and comments disclosed, and the amount of relevant information generated that informs collective research goals.
Output indicators for a podcast include the number of episode streams across all major podcast platforms and the level of engagement with educational materials.
Output indicators for a written piece include the amount of readership (recorded by the CSIS webpage), the number and quality of future citations made in reference to the written piece, and amount of engagement with educational materials.

target.value:
Increased conversations regarding resilient food systems and value chains within and across public and private organizations in the United States and Denmark. Ideas generated for program implementation and policy impact.
Participation of Danish and other policymakers in U.S. conversations on resilient food systems at CSIS and beyond.
References made in the media, press, and on the social media accounts of relevant stakeholders.
Project commences in Jan. 2024. Engagement signed in Dec. 2023.

Output indicators for a public event include in-person attendance and live viewership (online), continued viewership of event recordings, media presence, press mentions, engagement with educational materials, and references to the event discussion by experts in the field.
Output indicators for a private event include the number of public and private sector organizations represented during the discussion, the quality of the discussion and comments disclosed, and the amount of relevant information generated that informs collective research goals.

target.value: One private roundtable and one policy brief that looks at China, Russia, and other emergent donors approach in Africa. Two, how this conflicts with existing U.S. and West approach to development; and, Three, how to balance these competing development approaches.
Project commences in Jan. 2024. Engagement signed in Dec. 2023.
